items.detail: The **S&P 500 rose 2.51%** on the week to 7,561.67, its best week since August, while the Nasdaq gained 2.27% to 25,136.27 despite a down Friday.
items.why: Monday's 2.3% surge, the best day since April, came as Brent crude fell nearly 6% and chip stocks rebounded.

items.detail: October consumer prices rose **0.4%** in a month, above forecasts, and pushed the 10-year Treasury yield above 5% for the first time in a while.
items.why: Markets now fully price a December Fed hike, and Governor Waller floated a half-point move if inflation stays hot.

items.detail: Nvidia fell for a **sixth straight week**, and tech dragged Friday's session after CEO Jensen Huang resigned.
items.why: The leadership shock, following a board investigation, made investors question the AI trade's biggest name.

items.detail: MSCI's emerging-market stock index rose **nearly 4%** on the week, its first weekly gain since September, led by South Korea and Taiwan.
items.why: AI-heavy Asian chip stocks rebounded, while EM currencies held flat even as the dollar climbed.

items.detail: The **NIFTY 50 rose about 0.5%** to 25,144, its third straight weekly gain, with PSU banks leading and IT lagging.
items.why: Foreign investors kept buying, with about ₹79,300 crore of November inflows so far.

items.detail: India's **Nifty Smallcap 100 jumped 3.6%** on the week, its second straight weekly gain and well ahead of the NIFTY's 0.5%.
items.why: Strong foreign inflows and better risk appetite helped smaller domestic stocks outrun the large caps.

items.detail: Bitcoin slid from about $75,000 to **near $67,000**, falling below $69,000 on Friday as $1.26 billion of leveraged long bets were wiped out.
items.why: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost money for six straight sessions as Fed hike bets rose.

items.detail: Ether dropped **12.4%** on the week to about $1,958, falling back below $2,000.
items.why: Spot ether ETFs lost nearly $700 million in early November, and more holders queued to exit staking.

items.detail: Solana lost **about 10%** on the week to around $81, its lowest since mid-August, after breaking below its 200-day average.
items.why: Bitcoin's drop and heavy liquidations dragged down riskier coins, and the chart breakdown triggered more selling.

items.detail: Spot gold fell from about $4,070 last Friday to **below $3,900**, reversing the prior week's 5% gain.
items.why: The hot inflation report lifted Treasury yields and the dollar, which makes gold less attractive because it pays no interest.

crossCuttingTheme: Hotter October inflation made a December Fed hike look certain and pushed the 10-year yield above 5%, lifting the dollar; gold and crypto sold off, while stocks kept the gains from Monday's oil-driven rally.
